title: Level 3 (Advanced) - C-29
notes:
West leads the ♠7 against 3NT. South's only hope is that West's lead is away from the ♠K. The ♠3 is played from dummy and South wins the ♠Q. South must hope to establish the clubs, but he can only afford to lose the lead once. The defense will always have at least 1 club trick. South should try to maximize his chances of losing only 1 club trick.

South begins by ducking the first round of clubs. The defense wins and continues spades, won in dummy. A second round of clubs is played from dummy. When East follows with a club other than the ♣K, South must decide whether to play the ♣A or the ♣Q.

Playing the ♣A will be right when East began with 3 small clubs. Playing the ♣Q will be right when East began with 3 clubs to the ♣K. As the ♣K is more likely to be with length than with shortness, South should finesse the ♣Q.
